text:
meera: quick heads-up — bringing up reranker-v2 on staging and seeing a weird metric split. NDCG@10 improved ~0.8% but MRR@10 dropped ~1.2% on the same eval set. not a classic regressions signal, feels like tie / score calibration issue.
jia: can you paste the small repro stats? sample sizes, topk, any truncation?
meera: sure — eval params: topk=10, holdout=50k queries, doc_len_bins=[short,mid,long], tokenizer=hf-roberta. short queries (<=10 tokens): NDCG +1.5% but MRR -2.4%. long queries: both metrics +0.2%.
alex: hmm that pattern smells like ties at rank 1 for short queries — many docs same score after ptq or score quantization. how are ties broken in the harness today?
meera: current harness: stable_sort on candidate_id (insertion order). that means ordering depends on retrieval ordering. i think scoring collisions move different docs into top1 -> MRR sensitive, NDCG less so.
sam: can we reproduce deterministically by forcing tie-collapse and averaging? e.g. treat equal-scored candidates as a single bucket and use average reciprocal rank across permutations.
jeval-bot: CI rerank-eval run 1768123450 completed: ndcg_delta:+0.80% mrr_delta:-1.21% p_bootstrap(mrr)<0.05 -> 0.03 (1000 resamples) — see /ci/artifacts/1768123450.json
jia: meera, can you run Alex's bootstrap with tie-handling variants? quick command i use locally: ```python eval/ndcg_mrr.py --pred preds.json --gold gold.json --tie_strategy {stable,avg,random} --bootstrap 1000```
meera: running now, attaching diff summary in a sec.
lucy: also check label pooling — many annotations have pooled duplicates for short queries; if gold has multiple equivalent docs, MRR can flip depending on candidate order. i've seen this before in webqa sets.
alex: agree. two actionable checks: 1) rerun eval with tie_strategy=avg and random (seeded) and compare MRR; 2) add length-normalized score experiment: score' = score / (1 + 0.1 * doc_len_tokens) to see if long-doc bias is hiding.
sam: for (1) bootstrap comparison command i use: ```bash
python eval/bootstrap_compare.py \ 
  --pred preds.json \ 
  --gold gold.json \ 
  --metric mrr@10 --tie-strategies stable,avg,random \ 
  --resamples 1000 --seed 42
```
meera: quick results (local, 10k queries):
- stable: mrr=-1.18% (p=0.028)
- avg: mrr=-0.10% (p=0.48)
- random(seed=42): mrr=-0.14% (p=0.41)
so avg/random collapse the drop.
jia: that strongly indicates tie collisions from quantization/ptq. do we know score value distributions? any large mass at few discrete values?
meera: yes — histogram shows peaks at 0.512, 0.498, 0.384 — looks quantized. ran `np.unique(scores, return_counts=True)` and top counts show many identical values in topk.
alex: do we want to change default harness tie policy to avg? that yields more stable evaluation for model comparisons. also log tie fraction per query in dashboards.
lucy: +1 for avg as default for offline eval. but production ranking needs deterministic tie-breaker — keep stable for serving, but eval avg to avoid false regressions.
sam: proposal: update eval harness to support `--tie-strategy=avg` default for offline CI, add `tie_fraction` metric to ndcg/mrr outputs, and add a check that flags runs where tie_fraction>0.05.
meera: i'll open a PR for harness change and run full holdout. assigning: meera -> PR + full eval; alex -> add tie_fraction dashboard panel; sam -> add CI alert rule.
alex: thanks. also record this in release notes: "evaluation: tie-handling updated to average ties to reduce artifactual MRR regressions under score quantization".
meera: filing issue now. ping me if you need the exact histograms. :thumbsup:
